solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Participating in more than a wild goose chase

definitions.text: Participating in more than a wild goose chase

parts.words: Participating in more than a wild goose chase
parts.note: a hunting trip after big game is something grander than chasing one wild goose

explanation.walkthrough: A wild goose chase is a pointless errand; the clue turns it literal, a hunt for wild creatures, and a bigger one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a hunting or viewing expedition in the African bush is taking part in a chase after many wild animals.

clue.text: Gold fragments on paths

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
bits are small fragments

explanation.surface: Pieces of gold scattered along the walkways.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are the curved courses that planets and satellites travel, so they are paths.

clue.text: Pleasure in fraudulent London suburb

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other here

parts.note: sham means fake or fraudulent
a treat is a pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone finds enjoyment in a crooked corner of London.
explanation.walkthrough: STREATHAM is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Streatham is a residential district in the south of the capital, a London suburb.

clue.text: End of term activity before coming out?

definitions.text: End of term activity before coming out?

parts.words: End of term activity before coming out?
parts.note: an establishment that polishes young women before their debut in society, read as the last thing done before a term ends

explanation.walkthrough: Coming out here is a debutante's formal entry into society; 'End of term' suggests the last day at any school.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college teaching etiquette to girls prepared them for their society debut, the old 'coming out'.

clue.text: Toddler's bedtime story of a good baron in castle

indicators.note: in tells us the small pieces are placed inside the chess piece

parts.note: in chess the castle is also called a rook
B is an abbreviation for baron in peerage lists

explanation.surface: A child's goodnight tale about a kindly nobleman living in a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag book is a cloth picture book, hard to tear, made for very young children to handle.

clue.text: Shortly gauge drug ring

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Soon a meter will measure a drugs network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' is part of the definition: the answer is a short form of the name of the dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedo is the colloquial clipped name for a speedometer, the dial showing a vehicle's velocity.

clue.text: Maybe stop, turning up mountain track

indicators.note: turning the letters around mixes them into a new order

explanation.surface: Perhaps halt, turning back on the path up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb but is the full stop, one example of the answer, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is one example of a symbol used in writing to separate sentences, so it is a punctuation mark.

clue.text: It happened during the 70s

indicators.note: during tells us the answer lies within the spelt-out decade, so its outer letters and tail go

parts.note: the 70s are written out as the seventies

explanation.surface: Something took place in that decade.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out 'the 70s' as SEVENTIES and the answer sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that happened.

clue.text: Frequently takes papers after round

indicators.note: after places the newspapers behind the round letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
two newspapers: the FT and The Times

explanation.surface: Someone often buys the newspapers after finishing a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: The papers are the Financial Times (FT) and The Times, fitting in an FT puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft-times is an old-fashioned word meaning often or many times.

clue.text: Drivers should do so and keep quiet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fasten the seat belt
second meaning: a rude order to shut up

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is both a safety instruction in a car and a brusque command for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists must fasten their seat belts, and the phrase is also British slang for shut up.

clue.text: Nobleman at counter, working

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is busy behind a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage, a titled noble.

clue.text: Fourth grade judo award which will not attract development

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in many judo systems the fourth coloured belt is green
second meaning: protected countryside around a town where building is restricted

explanation.walkthrough: The green belt is protected land around British towns where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a mid-level coloured grade in martial arts, and planners keep rural land ringing a city free of new building.

clue.text: Travellers' delight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the vehicles and systems that travellers use; the clue gives it as a possessive
second meaning: a ... of delight is rapture

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes it read as one phrase; split it into what travellers use and an old word for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses and trains carry passengers, and in older usage strong emotion that carries one away is rapture.

clue.text: African expresses disapproval over Indian leader

indicators.note: over places the first piece ahead of the next one in an across answer

parts.note: tuts means clicks the tongue disapprovingly

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa clicks their tongue at an Indian politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Hikers' distressing call

indicators.note: distressing suggests the letters are agitated and thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Walkers in trouble give an alarming cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a high piercing cry, a kind of call.

clue.text: Publicity broadcast that is plain

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
to air something is to broadcast it
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Advertising that goes out on air is unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective but is the noun, an open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide grassy treeless plain of North America.

clue.text: Land of Hope

parts.note: the novelist Anthony Hope invented this kingdom for The Prisoner of Zenda

explanation.walkthrough: Hope is not an emotion but the author Anthony Hope; the phrase also echoes the song Land of Hope and Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional central European kingdom of Hope's adventure novel is the country belonging to that writer.

clue.text: The very best having a long time at The Feathers

parts.note: a plum job or role is the choicest one
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: The finest people spend hours at a pub called The Feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Feathers is a common British pub name, so the surface reads as a long session there.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's plumage is its covering of feathers.

clue.text: Go miles breaking porcelain

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Walking a long way risks smashing the china.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is the fine hard-paste china made in that French city.

clue.text: Arrest secret policemen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a standstill, as in cardiac arrest
second meaning: members of the Stasi, East Germany's secret police, taken as a plural

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' is a noun meaning a halt, not police detaining someone, though the second half tempts that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill or stoppage, and the East German security service was the Stasi.

clue.text: Civic announcement from them in tears?

definitions.text: Civic announcement from them in tears?

parts.words: Civic announcement from them in tears?
parts.note: town officials who shouted public news, and also people who are weeping

explanation.walkthrough: Town officials once called out public notices; people in tears are literally doing what the name says.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellmen who proclaimed news in the streets share a name with those who weep.

clue.text: Select group at lake bed, first

indicators.note: first puts the bed ahead of the lake

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An exclusive party gathers by a lakeside bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Wound up near Germany

parts.note: close means near
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone ended up somewhere close to the German border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' suggests annoyed, but it means concluded.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting that is wound up has been brought to an end, finished.

clue.text: Pompous dwarf's question about his identity?

definitions.text: Pompous dwarf's question about his identity?

parts.words: Pompous dwarf's question about his identity?
parts.note: Doc, one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, asking whether people mean him, which sounds like a Bordeaux wine region

explanation.walkthrough: Doc is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs; a self-important Doc might ask 'Me, Doc?'. Médoc is a red-wine area of Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful question splits into two words naming the Bordeaux district famous for its claret.

clue.text: Old tribe at church function

parts.note: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
CE abbreviates Church of England

explanation.surface: An ancient tribe arrives at a church event.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance is a social gathering, a function where people dance.

clue.text: Social worker, female, having short chat before baby is born

parts.note: the ant is a social insect and a worker
Ena is a female first name
talk with its last letter cut short

explanation.surface: A female social worker chats briefly with an expectant mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a care professional but the ant, a social insect; 'short' trims TALK to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal means relating to pregnancy, the period preceding birth.

clue.text: Boatman drooling drunkenly over last of ale

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests the letters stagger into a new order
last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Venetian oarsman slobbers tipsily over his beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola, the flat-bottomed boat on Venice's canals.

clue.text: Relatives — one of them seen in Taunton with leading spinner

parts.words: one of them seen in Taunton
parts.note: one relative, an aunt, can be spotted in the letters of Taunton

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A family member is spotted in Taunton beside the top spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is a Somerset county town with a cricket ground, which is why a spinner (spin bowler) fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are the sisters of a parent, family relations.

clue.text: A deception — initially, husband's upset woman

indicators.note: upset in a down light turns the string over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a lie is a deception
initially takes the first letter of husband, with its 's kept

explanation.surface: A trick involving her husband has left a woman distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEILA is Australian slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian and New Zealand slang a sheila is a girl or woman.

clue.text: Two sets of cards for one on board

parts.note: the first of the two sets of cards: a deck is a full pack
the second set of cards: a hand is the cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: Two packs of playing cards are needed for a single game aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two sets of cards' supplies both pieces: a deck and a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a crew member working on the deck of a ship, someone on board.
